name: decision-walk
title: Decision walk (branching scenario)
tagline: Branching 'choose-your-path' scenario — labelled options lead to outcome cards; drawn as a branching tree, static or staged; labels occludable.
description: A branching-decision scenario — a "choose your path" / decision-tree diagram. Decision boxes each pose a question and carry two-or-more labelled options; each option leads to the next decision or to a terminal outcome card (a title plus a short recommendation sentence). You author only the scenario — each decision with its options (a label and the id it leads to) and each outcome with its text — and the model derives every box position (a layered auto-layout, so converging paths merge into one box), the box sizes, every option arrow, the entry node, and — from a chosen `walk` — the highlighted route and a breadcrumb of the chosen option labels. The static render shows the whole map of choices (a faithful decision tree); set `walk` to highlight one route through it, and step that `walk` across staged `steps` to trace the route frame by frame. Any node or option label occludes to "?" for "which option / which outcome?", and nodes/edges highlight in amber. For an algorithm with loops and merging arrows use diagram/flowchart; for a static classification hierarchy with no walk use diagram/tree.
whenToUse: Reach for this to lay out a branching decision — a "choose your path" scenario, a decision tree, a routing/diagnostic flow, a "which method/strategy should I use?" guide. A question leads, via one of its options, to the next question and on to an outcome (a recommendation); a chosen route can be highlighted and traced. Author the scenario: list the nodes; a "decision" node has a `label` (the question) and an `options` array (each option a `label` and the id it leads `to`); an "outcome" node has a `label` (the result title) and an optional `detail` (the recommendation sentence). Positions, arrows, the entry point and the route are all derived, so you never place anything; two options may lead to the same node (the paths converge into one box). Set `start` to choose the entry decision (default: the node nothing points at). Static vs staged: leave `walk` off for the whole map; or set `walk` to an ordered list of node ids (entry first) and step it across `steps` to trace one route frame by frame (the chosen labels show as a breadcrumb, the route ambers). A staged `walk` build is frame-stable (the full map is always reserved). Questions: occlude a node's or an option's label to ask "which outcome does this path reach?" / "what choice leads here?" (the rest stays visible); highlight a node to mark the answer outcome. Keep the same scenario across the blocks of one lesson. Common maths uses: "which average — mean, median or mode?", "how should I solve this quadratic?", "is this number prime?", "what type of correlation?", classifying a quadrilateral by walking the questions; also careers routers, biology identification keys, any branching "if… then…" pathway. This is a teaching/illustration surface, not an auto-marked question (a graded "walk the route" response mode is not built). Switch model when the picture changes: a step-by-step algorithm with loops or arrows that merge back is diagram/flowchart; a static top-down classification you read rather than walk is diagram/tree; a single hub with one ring of ideas is diagram/mind-map. Synonyms a teacher might use: decision tree, branching scenario, choose your path, flow, pathway, routing, diagnostic, decision diagram, "which one should I use", identification key, choose-your-own-adventure.

id.description: Unique kebab-case id for this node, referenced by options' `to` and by `start`/`walk` (e.g. "enjoy-maths", "outcome-median"). Not shown to pupils — the wiring handle.

kind.description: What this node is. "decision" → a question box that branches (give it an `options` array). "outcome" → a terminal result card (no options; carries a `label` title and an optional `detail` recommendation sentence). The shape and colour are derived from this.

label.description: The text inside the box, wrapped to fit. A decision's label is the question ("Is the data skewed?"); an outcome's label is the result title ("Use the median").

detail.description: OUTCOME ONLY — a short recommendation/explanation sentence drawn under the outcome title ("Resistant to outliers, so it represents a skewed set best."). Wraps inside the card. Ignored on a decision. Default none.

label.description: The choice text drawn on this option's arrow (e.g. "Higher education", "Yes, I enjoy it", "Score ≥ 70"). Wraps to fit; keep it short — the rich description belongs on the outcome it leads to.

to.description: Id of the node this option leads to — the next decision, or an outcome. Must name a node in this list. Two options may point at the SAME node (paths converge — drawn as one merged box).

occlude.description: Render this option's label as "?" — the "which choice leads here?" hook. The arrow stays drawn and the hidden word never leaks into the aria. Default false.

highlight.description: Amber this option's arrow — mark the answer route, or trace a chosen branch. Usually you instead set `walk` and let the chosen route highlight itself. Default false.

options.description: DECISION ONLY — the choices leaving this question, each a label + the id it leads to. Give a real decision two or more. Ignored on an outcome.

occlude.description: Render this node's label (and an outcome's detail) as "?" — the "what question / which outcome goes here?" hook. The box and arrows stay drawn; the hidden words never leak into the aria. Default false.

highlight.description: Amber this node — the answer outcome, or a box on a traced route. When `walk` is set the chosen route highlights itself, so use this only for a static "the answer is here" figure. Default false.

color.description: Override THIS node's BASE colour (decision boxes default blue, outcome cards teal). Wins over the figure-wide `colors.decisions`/`colors.outcomes`. IMPORTANT: the walked-route highlight and the breadcrumb stay amber regardless (the chosen path is reserved), and a highlighted node stays amber — `color` only affects the un-walked, un-highlighted appearance. A reserved role keyword (accent, accent-2…accent-5, ink, muted, scaffold) keeps it brand-themeable; a colour literal (#hex, rgb()/rgba(), hsl()/hsla(), or a CSS named colour) is honoured exactly and opts this box OUT of brand reskinning.

nodes.description: The nodes of the scenario: decision boxes (a question + an `options` array) and outcome cards (a title + optional `detail`). Order does not matter — positions are derived from the options. Give the scenario at least one decision and one outcome.

start.description: Id of the entry decision (where the walk begins). Optional — defaults to the node nothing points at (the root); set it when the auto-detected entry is ambiguous.

walk.description: An ordered list of node ids (entry first) naming a chosen route — the model highlights that route, shows a breadcrumb of the chosen option labels and marks the frontier (last node). Use it to TRACE one path, stepping it across staged `steps` (["start"], ["start","a"], ["start","a","out"]). Leave it off for the whole map.

direction.description: Reading flow: "down" (default) lays the scenario top-to-bottom; "right" lays a short one left-to-right. Keep it consistent across a lesson.

showBreadcrumb.description: Show the "Your path: A › B › C" strip of chosen option labels below the figure when a `walk` is set (or being walked). Default true.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure; the top padding grows to clear it.

caption.description: Optional line centred below the figure, e.g. a short context note. Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.

colors.description: Optional figure-wide colour overrides — set ONLY on an explicit author/teacher request. These recolour the BASE appearance only; the walked-route highlight, the breadcrumb and any `highlight` stay amber (reserved). A per-node `color` overrides these for one box.

decisions.description: Default colour of every (un-walked) decision box, replacing accent blue. A reserved role keyword (accent, accent-2…accent-5, ink, muted, scaffold) stays brand-themeable; a colour literal (#hex, rgb()/rgba(), hsl()/hsla(), or a CSS named colour like "teal") is honoured exactly.

outcomes.description: Default colour of every (un-reached) outcome card, replacing teal. Same value space as `decisions`. A reached outcome stays amber (the result is reserved).

options.description: Default colour of the (un-walked) option arrows and their labels, replacing the construction grey. Same value space as `decisions`.

nodes.label: Mean
nodes.detail: Add every value and divide by how many there are; best for even numerical data because it uses all of it.

nodes.label: Median
nodes.detail: Order the values and take the middle one; it ignores how extreme the ends are, so outliers and skew do not distort it, and it still works for ranked categories.

nodes.label: Mode
nodes.detail: The most frequent value; the only average that makes sense when the data are just names.
